dedupe_keys.name: eia hourly demand screening and mice imputation code

description: This preparation workflow screens and imputes hourly US electricity-demand observations before their use in power-system models. The Carnegie Institution for Science team publishes four notebook stages: query the EIA database, screen anomalies, apply Multiple Imputation by Chained Equations, and distribute results to balancing-authority and aggregate files. Python handles acquisition and distribution while R and the mice package perform imputation. GitHub and the Zenodo code archive state MIT, allowing free reuse. Coverage follows the input observations; the documented project cleaned the contiguous US series, not implementing an electricity simulator itself. It can prepare demand inputs for dispatch and capacity-planning models, comparable in purpose to the input series in data-re-europe. A caveat is that fresh acquisition requires an EIA API key and historical source values can change. The preserved companion Conda environment targets macOS 10.14.6; portability and current API compatibility were not tested. No software archive was downloaded or environment installed.
